title: cluster-readiness output data
description:
Shape of the ``data`` field on a ``cluster-readiness`` envelope.

``render`` rides the result the way it does on ``attention-queue`` — the
agent relays it VERBATIM. The single ``computed_at`` stamp dates the whole
projection and is the instant every age was measured against.

computed_at.description: The single instant readiness was computed against (ISO-8601 UTC).
computed_at.title: Computed At

clusters.description: One entry per cluster/host, ordered by (cluster or '', host).
clusters.title: Clusters

counts.description: Entry count per overall verdict ({ready, stale, degraded, unknown}).
counts.title: Counts

render.description: The deterministic markdown digest — relayed to the human verbatim.
render.title: Render

ClusterReadinessEntry.description: The readiness of one cluster (or one bare host with a ledger).

cluster.description: The clusters.yaml key, or null for a host with a ledger but no config entry.
cluster.title: Cluster

host.description: The ssh host key the ledger is filed under.
host.title: Host

verdict.description: ready / stale / degraded / unknown — the single overall verdict computed from the atoms below by state/readiness.overall_verdict.
verdict.title: Verdict

atoms.description: Recorded atoms ordered by (sensor position, route, target), each followed by an 'unknown' placeholder for every sensor kind nothing has fed — absence is emitted, never omitted.
atoms.title: Atoms

ledger_corrupt.description: True when the ledger file existed but could not be read. The entry then reports an EMPTY ledger (verdict 'unknown') and says so — a corrupt file is disclosed, never a crash and never silently green.
ledger_corrupt.title: Ledger Corrupt

ledger_corruption_reason.description: Why this read could not use the file (unreadable / not valid JSON / not a JSON object / no usable schema_version / schema_version newer than this build / atoms is not a list); null when it read cleanly.
ledger_corruption_reason.title: Ledger Corruption Reason

ledger_last_corruption.description: {at, reason} for a PREVIOUS ledger file that a write discarded as unreadable. Persisted through the rebuild so the operator learns once that something was lost, instead of the disclosure vanishing with the file the moment any traffic touches the host.
ledger_last_corruption.title: Ledger Last Corruption

ClusterReadinessEntry.title: cluster-readiness entry

ReadinessAtomModel.description:
One verdict atom: what was probed, over which route, when, and how long.

The wire projection of ``infra/readiness_sensors.VerdictAtom`` plus the two
derived reading aids (``age_seconds``, ``stale``) and the durable tier's
additive ``source``.

A sensor that nothing has fed is still emitted, with ``verdict='unknown'``
and every other field null — absence is reported, not omitted, so a reader
can never mistake an unfed invariant for a green one.

sensor.description: What was probed: hop / direct / path / connect / preamble (the sensor layer's vocabulary), extended by the durable ledger with auth / scratch / scheduler / env.
sensor.title: Sensor

target.description: The chain element or host the reading is about (a hop's own hostname, or the target); null when no observation exists.
target.title: Target

route.description: Which route the reading was taken over: 'effective' (what ssh -G resolved, hops included), 'direct' (hop-bypassing — the discriminator for a dead ProxyJump), or 'n/a'. Null when unknown.
route.title: Route

verdict.description: ok / down / timeout / unknown / skipped as recorded, or 'unknown' when no observation of this sensor exists. 'unknown' means the sensor could not settle it and 'skipped' means it never ran — neither is 'fine'.
verdict.title: Verdict

at.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the observation was recorded; null when unknown.
at.title: At

age_seconds.description: Age of the observation at computed_at, in whole seconds; null when unknown or when the stamp is unparseable.
age_seconds.title: Age Seconds

stale.description: True when the observation is past this sensor's freshness horizon (or has no usable stamp, or does not exist). A stale verdict is never read as current — that assertion is the whole point.
stale.title: Stale

stale_after_seconds.description: This sensor's freshness horizon in seconds, so the age reads against it.
stale_after_seconds.title: Stale After Seconds

latency_ms.description: The observation's own measured duration, when the site held one; null otherwise. Never estimated.
latency_ms.title: Latency Ms

source.description: Durable-tier provenance naming the seam that recorded it (rendered, never interpreted); not part of VerdictAtom.
source.title: Source

detail.description: The reading's own short opaque note; null when it recorded none.
detail.title: Detail

ReadinessAtomModel.title: cluster-readiness atom
